clue.text: Guarding relic of criminal mastermind

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters of the words before it are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A guard keeps watch over some relic left behind by a master criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like part of the definition, but it is the anagram signal: GUARDINGRELICOF rearranges into the Bond villain's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's villain plots the raid on Fort Knox, the very model of a scheming criminal brain.

clue.text: Like Sidney's romance song about rogue knight

indicators.note: about says the song goes round the rogue

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
a cad is a rogue or bounder
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A ballad from Philip Sidney's pastoral romance tells of a scoundrel knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Philip Sidney's prose romance is the Arcadia, so anything like it is pastoral in this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney's romance is set in Arcadia, an idealised pastoral land, so something like it is rustic and idyllic.

clue.text: Screenwriter perhaps writing on Monday, staggering friend from TV

parts.note: R stands for writing as one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

indicators.note: staggering means reeling, so the letters of the day are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Chandler Bing is one of the six characters in the sitcom Friends

explanation.surface: A screenwriter starts work on a Monday, tottering like a sitcom character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' is the anagram signal for the day's name. 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: the novelist also co-wrote the film Double Indemnity.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime novelist also wrote Hollywood scripts, such as Double Indemnity, making him one example of a film writer.

clue.text: Cows with love for a man behind Malvern Hills

indicators.note: love for a says the letter a is replaced by the love letter

parts.note: cows are cattle
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Cattle graze lovingly beneath the Malvern Hills, watched by a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Cottle, the Bristol publisher of Lyrical Ballads, wrote a poem called Malvern Hills. 'with love for a' swaps an A of CATTLE for O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bristol bookseller and poet wrote the long poem Malvern Hills, so he is the author standing behind that work.

clue.text: Author's follow-up to November sounded mad

parts.note: in the NATO alphabet November is followed by Oscar

indicators.note: sounded says the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: wild can mean mad or furious

explanation.surface: A writer's sequel to a book called November is said to be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Author stands for is, a link. November is the radio-alphabet word for N, and the next letter's word is Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright of The Importance of Being Earnest is a famous writer.

clue.text: 24's friend who changes colour

definitions.meaning: George ... was a close friend of Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia
a person who tints cloth for a living

explanation.walkthrough: 24 refers to the answer at 24 down, the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: George Dyer, the scholar, was Lamb's friend; and a cloth tinter is a tradesman who gives fabric new colours.

clue.text: Popular outlet with men such as John Galt

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a vent is an outlet for air or steam
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A trendy shop for men stocks the novels of the Scottish writer John Galt.
explanation.walkthrough: John Galt is also a Scottish novelist, but here he is the hero of Ayn Rand's Atlas Shrugged, who built a revolutionary motor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayn Rand's John Galt designs a new kind of engine, so he is an example of a creator of new machines.

clue.text: Writer adapted farce of e.g. Hue and Cry

indicators.note: adapted means altered for a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author turned the Ealing comedy Hue and Cry into a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges FARCEOFEGHUE plus CRY; the 'and' is only a link. Hue and Cry is a 1947 British film comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Canterbury Tales is a medieval English poet.

clue.text: Mother of little devil losing heart for prayers

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters are dropped

parts.note: in Rosemary's Baby the heroine gives birth to the son of Satan

explanation.surface: A mother despairs of her naughty child and turns to prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes the middle EM out of ROSEMARY. 'little devil' reads as a naughty child, but it is the baby in Ira Levin's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a set sequence of Catholic devotions, counted on beads.

clue.text: Reveal sadness in verse, avoiding Old English — like this?

parts.note: to show sorrow is to cry

indicators.note: avoiding says the letters for Old English are kept out of the word before

parts.note: written in verse means poetic

explanation.surface: A poet lays bare their grief in verse while steering clear of archaic language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes OE out of POETIC, leaving PTIC. The definition points at the clue itself, which is one of its own kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is itself a puzzle with hidden wordplay, the kind of clue this whole crossword is made of.

clue.text: Begrudging audience with sides splitting after parts two and three of Henry VI

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the letters before it

parts.words: parts two and three of Henry
parts.note: the second and third letters of the name Henry

indicators.note: the sides of a word splitting off means its first and last letters leave

parts.note: a theatre's audience is its house

explanation.surface: A theatregoer resents the laughing crowd at the later parts of Shakespeare's Henry VI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with sides splitting' drops the first and last letters of the theatre word. 'Henry VI' sounds like Shakespeare's history plays, but only its second and third letters and the numeral are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone begrudging resents another's good fortune, which is exactly what jealousy of that kind is.

clue.text: Humour and depth resembling The Waves?

parts.note: waves at sea are rollers, so something like them is roller-y, a made-up word flagged by the question mark

explanation.surface: A critic says Virginia Woolf's novel The Waves blends wit and profundity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Waves is Virginia Woolf's novel, but here it means sea waves, which are rollers; the question mark admits the invented adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is whimsical, dry wit, a synonym for comic humour.

clue.text: Brutus, say, about to be a traitor from behind

indicators.note: read from behind means the letters are taken backwards

parts.note: re means about, as in a letter heading
to fink is to inform or betray, American slang

explanation.surface: Brutus is on the point of betraying Caesar by stabbing him in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' turns the whole run REFINK backwards. Brutus fits the surface's traitor, but the definition calls him a stabber.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus joined the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar, so he is a man wielding a blade.

clue.text: Gone with the Wind's lead message covering fun time girl

indicators.note: covering says one piece goes round the others

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message
a lark is a bit of fun
G is an abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: A telegram tells of a party girl having a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals the telegram wrapping round the rest. G for girl is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: He played Rhett Butler, the male star of the 1939 film, opposite Vivien Leigh.

clue.text: Support American opera

parts.note: to support is to aid

explanation.surface: Someone backs an opera company in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's work set in ancient Egypt is one of the best-known operas.

clue.text: Dorothea's love that hurts, breaking a resolution

parts.note: Dorothea Brooke in George Eliot's Middlemarch falls for Will Ladislaw

indicators.note: breaking says one piece splits the other open

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
ow is what one says when something hurts

explanation.surface: A heroine's painful romance shatters her firm resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' signals the cry of pain splitting the word for 'a', used as in 'so much a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution in the sense of firm determination is strength of mind to keep to a purpose.

clue.text: Setting for Revolutionary Road is B&B outside city, once taken by great American in retirement

indicators.note: taken by says the first part is held inside the second
in retirement means drawing back, so the pair are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I

indicators.note: outside says the two letters sit round the city

parts.note: two B's, the letters as written
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Richard Yates's novel is set in a guesthouse beyond the city, once bought by an American in his retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns AIUS into SUIA, and 'taken by' puts BURB inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yates's novel follows a couple stifled in 1950s Connecticut commuter suburbs.

clue.text: Ruby Ferguson initially broke it to her

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the word Ferguson
broke means shattered, so the three words after it are scrambled

explanation.surface: The children's writer Ruby Ferguson gently told a girl some bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby Ferguson wrote the Jill pony books, but 'Ruby' alone is the definition. 'broke' rearranges ITTOHER into ORTIETH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby wedding marks forty years of marriage, so ruby stands for the anniversary of that number.

clue.text: "This is our master, famous, calm and dead / Borne on our -" (A Grammarian's Funeral, Robert Browning)

definitions.text: "This is our master, famous, calm and dead / Borne on our -" (A Grammarian's Funeral, Robert Browning)

parts.words: "This is our master, famous, calm and dead / Borne on our -" (A Grammarian's Funeral, Robert Browning)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the dead scholar's pupils carry his body up the mountain on the upper parts of their bodies

explanation.definitionFit: Browning's mourners carry their master's coffin raised on the tops of their backs, the body part that bears a load.

clue.text: Reminder of Italian author broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: Umberto Eco is the Italian author of The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: A radio programme recalls an Italian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is something that brings back a memory of an earlier thing, a reminder of it.

clue.text: Revolutionary Polish spy series

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine Marxist revolutionary
to polish is to rub

explanation.surface: A Polish insurgent stars in a run of espionage stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb. 'Revolutionary' suggests reversal, yet it gives CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Muchamore's novels about teenage secret agents are a series named after that word.

clue.text: Originally, Martin Cruz Smith wasn't only one changing Gorky Park's location

indicators.note: changing means the gathered letters are put in a new order
originally means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Martin Cruz Smith, author of Gorky Park, was not alone in moving where the novel was set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' gives MCSWOO and 'changing' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorky Park is a large public park in the Russian capital, where Smith's thriller is set.

clue.text: Time to hold Japanese drama in high regard

indicators.note: to hold says the first word is wrapped round the second

parts.note: an hour is a period of time
No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: It is time to accord Japanese theatre the esteem it deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Honour as a noun means great respect or esteem shown to someone.

clue.text: Books on Lucrezia de' Medici, say, unopened and unread

indicators.note: on in an across clue says this piece comes after the other
unopened means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: an Italian noblewoman is a signora
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Volumes about a Medici duchess sit with their pages uncut and never read.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncut, unopened books suggest the definition is about the volumes, but 'unread' describes a person who has not read much.
explanation.definitionFit: An unread person is poorly educated, lacking knowledge gained from reading.

clue.text: Lamb's head removed by TV cook

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the essayist Charles Lamb is the answer

indicators.note: head removed means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British television cook

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef cuts the head off a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is the essayist Charles Lamb, whose pen name this is, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb published his Essays of Elia under this pseudonym.

clue.text: Give another name to Frankenstein's workplace in section of film

indicators.note: in says the lab piece goes inside the film section

parts.note: a reel is one section of a film
Victor Frankenstein builds his creature in a laboratory, or lab

explanation.surface: A film editor retitles the laboratory scene in one reel of a horror picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To rename something is to attach a new tag or label to it.

clue.text: It might be given to Rider Haggard by Cecil

definitions.text: It might be given to Rider

indicators.note: haggard first meant a wild, untamed hawk, so it signals the words after it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A present for the novelist H. Rider Haggard from a friend called Cecil.
explanation.walkthrough: Rider Haggard is the novelist, but split apart 'Rider' is a cyclist and 'Haggard', wild, is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist is a rider, and a bike is the machine you hand to someone who rides.

clue.text: Sculptor's block reflected horse — horse with record value

definitions.note: the 's stands for has: the sculptor has the wordplay that follows

parts.note: a bar is a block, as of soap or gold

indicators.note: reflected means seen in a mirror, so the word comes back to front

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse
an EP is an extended-play record
worth means value

explanation.surface: A sculptor's lump of stone is mirrored by a carved horse, then horse again, worth a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns ARAB into BARA. The second 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Barbara Hepworth was a British modernist sculptor famous for pierced abstract forms.
